Requirements
Transcripts
Domestic Transcripts: You may submit unofficial transcripts with your application.
Official transcripts will be required upon admission to a graduate program.
International Transcripts: Must be evaluated through a course-by-course transcript
evaluation from a NACES-approved organization (e.g., ECE, TEC - formerly SpanTran,
WES). The evaluation must include an original copy of your official transcript as
received by the evaluating agency. Please allow adequate time for evaluation processing
(typically 8+ weeks).
GPA
3.0 (on a 4.0 scale)
Personal Statement
For Nursing D.N.P. applicants, your personal statement must consist of the following:
What current healthcare trend(s) or social determinants of health (SDOH) impacting
your community are most concerning? After graduation, how do you envision your advanced
nursing role influencing the healthcare concern you have identified? What steps can
you take to address it through your leadership?
Instructions: Submit a two - to three-page (excluding title and reference pages) written
essay addressing the question(s) provided. The submission should demonstrate critical
thinking, academic integrity, and readiness for graduate-level writing. Your response
must be entirely your own work without the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and
demonstrate clear, professional, and well-organized writing.
Use 12-point Times New Roman font, double-spacing, and 1-inch margins.
American Psychological Association (APA) format is required (current edition) including
title page, in-text citations, and a reference list.
Incorporate at least two scholarly references to support your response.
Additional Requirements
An unencumbered license to practice as a Registered Nurse in United States
A Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN to DNP option) and/or a Master of Science in
Nursing (MSN to DNP option) from a program accredited by the National League for Nursing
Accrediting Commission (NLNAC) or the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).
Certification (for MSN to DNP applicants) in the selected nursing specialty for the
concentration (for instance, a FNP certification for the FNP concentration); at least
one year of experience in a nursing administration role for the Executive Leadership
concentration.
At least a “B” average (3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale) in the nursing major.
A curriculum vitae (CV) or resume.
Completion of an interview with ETSU faculty.
*Note: Review specific admission requirements for each concentration in the Graduate Catalog

Transcripts
Domestic Transcripts: You may submit unofficial transcripts with your application.

(typically 8+ weeks).
GPA
3.0 (on a 4.0 scale)
Personal Statement
Based on your nursing experience, discuss a possible researchable nursing problem,
including implications for nursing practice. Essay should be typewritten, double-spaced,
and at least 2 pages but not more than 4 pages in length. Include at least two scholarly
references. American Psychological Association (APA) format is required (current edition).
Additional Requirements
An unencumbered license to practice as a Registered Nurse in United States.
A Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) and a non-nursing Master’s degree OR a Master
of Science in Nursing (MSN) from a program accredited by the National League for Nursing
Accrediting Commission (NLNAC) or the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE)
OR a Doctor of Nursing Practice Degree (DNP).
Exceptional candidates with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) may be considered
for admission but will have a longer program of study and will earn the Master of
Science in Nursing (MSN) en route to the PhD.
At least a “B” average (3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale) in the nursing major.
A cover letter expressing the applicant’s personal goals for doctoral study and a
curriculum vitae (CV) or resume.
Completion of an interview with ETSU faculty.

The deadlines below are for completing the supplemental Graduate School application and pertain to those applicants recommended for admission by the Department.
Applicants must first apply through SOPHAS before the SOPHAS published deadline. Once the Department recommends a candidate,
they are provided with instructions for completing the supplemental Graduate School
application.
Graduate School applications will only be processed once a complete SOPHAS application
is submitted and a Departmental recommendation for admission is issued.
